verdict.rationale: Outlook is fully programmable through the documented Microsoft Graph mail API. The docs cover drafting, reading, replying to, sending and deleting messages, plus attachments, inbox rules, mailbox settings, sync, querying and change notifications, and the API works from any language that can send HTTP requests. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of agents driving Outlook via the API (the only community mention is a vague MCP/cloud search integration), and a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (the probes found none at the checked learn.microsoft.com paths).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Draft, read, reply, forward, send, update, or delete messages
With the information in this guide, you can implement this in any language or platform capable of sending HTTP requests.
Apps can set up [Inbox rules](/en-us/graph/api/resources/messagerule) to promptly handle incoming messages and reduce email clutter.
Get or update a user's automatic reply, locale, time zone, or working hours
Change notifications enable applications to receive alerts when a Microsoft Graph resource they're interested in changes; that is, created, updated, or deleted.
